# Independent review: source reflection preflight

Verdict: ACCEPT_SPECIFIED_SOURCE_REFLECTION_OBSTRUCTIONS_ONLY.
Candidate: SOURCE_REFLECTION_PREFLIGHT.md, 10687 bytes, SHA256
0740c57d7804ad7d0bb616f21240eed52e61de2dda7945367b2a8389e9571615.
Source base: f736bbe6feff383bd8fc76b72cc5a7cab031fe27.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review. Date: 2026-09-17.

R1--R12 are mathematically sound in the stated scope. No correction is
required. This rejects the specified inversion pairing on actual projected
signals and the specified copy-exchange Gram identification, including its
nonzero node factors and PSD tensor multipliers. It does not supply a
negative row of original V, an improved lower bound for V, or an RH claim.

## Direct sources and checks

The complete candidate was read and independently hashed. Named reports
were inspected directly; previously read unchanged density/conditional
inputs were rebound by their hashes in this pass. Input hashes are:

- BROWNIAN_DILATION_CONDITIONAL:
  8ea7ed0b70f57d271b09cb44f53156cd50b71aa6511bd1fd4077111ba5bef5ef.
- BROWNIAN_PRIMITIVE_FORM (including B8):
  00b5e80a573bd3a31c28f21ffa4fcf11695746c7df56274d12c0a94370e225fa.
- ANALYTIC_POSITIVITY_PROPAGATION (full A1--A3 proof):
  fb83c216aef4687425074732904f9d2f52aac77527a926e7556fb0067335e2bd.
- WEIL_ROSATI_TRANSFER_AUDIT (including sections 2--3):
  11bcc8b0208ea8e992312c43f5428de602b10e4c200c99b86bfef34afc580754.
- CONDITIONAL_CONNECTION (published C1--C18 and acceptance):
  2aa3c9dcd948045ee21dbc0f530fa73037968dce40d8c4592bedd48aed1757c9.
- NULLVAR raw response, complete h series and bounds (8)--(17):
  4fa7909725d2fa10ccc52d3413580289692d3a1489ecae7bed88956f80980730.

The full theta facts and previously accepted B8/A1 are named inputs.
No external theorem is newly imported. No search, numerical theta
quadrature/scan, descendant, dispatch, or repository write was performed.
The canonical read-only plan remains HOLD, ACTIVE control, no fatal error,
writes_performed=false. Only this assigned staging review is written.

## 1. R2 really uses two admissible source signals

Since dnu_X=(A/Z)f(X)dX, the squared H norms of m_x and its x derivative
are constant multiples of the integrals of f(X+x)^2/f(X) and
f'(X+x)^2/f(X). For |x|<=delta<log(2)/2, the full positive-tail estimates
have double-exponential coefficient at least 2exp(-2delta)-1>0. Evenness
handles the negative tail; derivative polynomial factors are absorbed by
the strict exponential gap. This supplies the asserted common integrable
majorants, H differentiability, and continuous derivative.

Thus m_0=1, m'_0=q=f'/f, and (m_(-h)-m_(-2h))/h converges in H to q.
The latter is odd and nonzero, with finite strictly positive squared norm.
The even probability makes J unitary and self-adjoint, so continuity of
the bounded reflected pairing gives exactly -I_rad in the limit.
For sufficiently small positive h both nodes are in I. This proves
negativity on the actual projected signal span, not only on an arbitrary
odd test. J need not preserve that restricted span for its pairing to be
well defined there. No assertion about original V's sign follows.

## 2. R3--R4 physical measure and exact Jacobian

Copy exchange preserves the joint measure and physical weight, and each
g_x is symmetric in its two energy variables. Therefore the reflected
form on this family is exactly its ordinary weighted Gram form R3.
The conditional integration of the physical measure gives f(X)^2 dX,
so neither the original weight nor normalization is replaced.

For T=u+v and s=u/T,

    dX ds = du dv/(2T^2),
    f(X)^2 = T^(5/2)r(T)^2/A^2,
    p_X(s) = T h(u)h(v)/r(T).

Multiplying both likelihoods first gives T^(7/2)r(T)/A^2 times the
h-ratio; then the Jacobian gives T^(3/2)r(T)/(2A^2). The factor
(ab)^(9/4) and exact cutoff T>=1 in R4 are correct.

For fixed real a,b in (0,1), large-coordinate exponentials combine to
exp(-pi(a+b)T). Near either zero endpoint the net reciprocal coefficient
is 1/a+1/b-1>0. Polynomial factors are integrable against these positive
exponential gaps. Hence the carrier is finite for all negative shifts,
including those outside the initially sufficient I domain.

## 3. Full complex analyticity on the negative strip

If z is in Omega, a=exp(2z) has Re(a)>0 and
Re(1/a)=exp(-2Re z)cos(2Im z)>1/2. On compact pairs in Omega x Omega,
Re(a+b) and Re(1/a+1/b)-1 have uniform strictly positive lower bounds.
The complete small-argument series then gives, for example,

    |h(au)h(bu)/h(u)|
      <= C u^(-N) exp[-pi(Re(1/a+1/b)-1)/(4u)]

near u=0. The real denominator has the matching positive lower
asymptotic. Large-coordinate series combined with r(T) give the strictly
positive tail gap above. Intermediate compact coordinates are harmless.
These estimates patch to a common integrable majorant for the entire
R4 integral. The prefactor is unambiguously exp((9/2)(z+w)).
Thus joint holomorphy on the stated product domain is justified, not
merely separate pointwise analyticity on the real axis.

## 4. R5--R7 scaling and overlap limit

Under (u,v)=(U/a,V/a), the powers outside J are

    a^(9/2) * a^(-3/2) * a^(-2) = a.

Also r(T/a)/(h(U/a)h(V/a)) is exactly
J(T/a)/(chi(U/a)chi(V/a)). This reproduces the bracket aJ and every
constant in R5, with the transformed cutoff T>=a.

For a<=1, monotonicity and J(t)<=t bound that bracket by
T/(chi(U)chi(V)). Multiplying h(U)h(V) cancels the denominator to
4pi^2 exp(-pi T). The stated positive dominating function follows.
It is integrable even using only boundedness of h(kappa U), h(kappa V),
because the remaining polynomial is integrated against exp(-pi T).
Pointwise aJ(T/a)->T and both chi denominators tend to 1. Therefore
R5 converges by dominated convergence over the whole quadrant; no sharp
cutoff contribution was silently discarded.

Both diagonal limits equal L(1)/(2A^2), since replacing x by x+d only
replaces a by kappa a, which also tends to zero. L is finite and strictly
positive. Hence the normalized limit is exactly L(kappa)/L(1).
The pinned B8 gives the original V limit sech(d) at the positive end;
V(-x,-y)=V(x,y) and evenness of sech give R7 at the negative end.
The two limits concern full integrals, not one endpoint or one mode.

## 5. R8--R9 uniform overlap decay and limit order

The proposed global upper bound for h follows by absorbing its small-u
polynomial into the strict gap pi/4-alpha and using the large-u gap
pi-beta, with compact continuity in between. Alpha=pi/8, beta=pi/2
are valid fixed positive choices.

For kappa>=1, AM--GM gives
A_k/u+(B_k/2)u>=sqrt(2A_k B_k)>=sqrt(2alpha beta kappa),
while B_k/2>=beta/2. Applying this to both U and V yields the displayed
kappa-independent majorant. The remaining integral equals

    integral_0^infinity T^(7/2)exp(-beta T/2)dT
      =Gamma(9/2)(2/beta)^(9/2),

because the length of the slice U+V=T is T. Thus R9 has the correct
Gamma power and c=2sqrt(2alpha beta)=pi/sqrt(2).
Since sech(d)=2sqrt(kappa)/(1+kappa), the ratio tends to zero.
The order of limits is legitimate: first select one sufficiently large
but fixed d from this bound, then apply the a->0 limit for that fixed d.
No uniform-in-d dominated convergence or exchanged double limit is used.

## 6. R10--R12 arbitrary multiplier and thin-rectangle propagation

Strict positivity of every real K entry is immediate from R4. Original
V entries are also strictly positive: set m=(x+y)/2, d=(x-y)/2 and use
the evenness of f(u+d)f(u-d) to write the integral from |m| to infinity
with positive weight 2u. Thus both normalized real overlaps in R11 are
well defined and real analytic throughout the connected negative quadrant.

Node factors alone leave absolute normalized overlaps unchanged. Their
hypothesized identity on I therefore forces equality of the two real
analytic normalized overlaps there and hence on the whole quadrant.
The established limiting mismatch contradicts this.

For arbitrary PSD M, diagonal positivity in R10 forces M(x,x)>0 and
eta(x)!=0. Write d(x)=eta(x)/|eta(x)|. Normalization gives

    R(x,y)=conjugate(d(x))d(y) M(x,y)/sqrt(M(x,x)M(y,y)).

This is PSD on I by diagonal congruence. No regularity of d, eta or M
is needed: this expression is forced to equal the explicit analytic R.
Its real diagonal is identically one.

To apply A1 correctly, fix a nonempty source subinterval strictly inside
I and any desired finite negative target nodes. Choose ONE compact
negative interval containing both, with a small negative real margin.
The continuous positive K has a strictly positive minimum on its square.
Compactness and the product holomorphic domain therefore provide a thin
complex rectangle around that interval whose full product has no K zero.
The positive real diagonal functions V(z,z), K(z,z) likewise have
nonvanishing positive-branch square roots on a sufficiently thin common
rectangle. Hence the entire ratio R11 is holomorphic on its product.

A1 now applies exactly, including mixed old/new Gram blocks, from the
fixed source subinterval to the selected finite nodes. The rectangle
may depend on those nodes; no uniform width at minus infinity is needed.
Consequently presumed PSD on I would imply R PSD at every finite negative
family. Its two-node minors then require |R(x,y)|<=1.

For the fixed d selected above, R(x,x+d) tends to sech(d)/C(d)>1.
This contradicts that necessary inequality. A1 does not claim an
explicit rank or two-node counterexample INSIDE I; none is claimed by
the candidate. It suffices to exclude all-family PSD there. The argument
therefore rules out arbitrary PSD tensor multipliers in R10, not only
analytic multipliers or finite-dimensional auxiliary features.

## Scope and final verdict

The first obstruction is a negative reflected form of two actual means.
The second is a mismatch between an independently positive full-likelihood
carrier and the original V, persistent under node congruences and positive
tensor factors. These are different forms from V itself. No original
negative witness is produced, and two-node V positivity is not contradicted.

The proof does not exclude other reflections with other maps, nonlocal
signal/scale mixing, direct sums with other fields, a different identity,
or positivity of V. In particular, it is not an all-reflection or all-
positive-carrier no-go theorem. No generic new request or canonical
admission follows. Full V positivity and RH remain open.

Final verdict: ACCEPT_SPECIFIED_SOURCE_REFLECTION_OBSTRUCTIONS_ONLY.
accepted: R2: source inversion pairing is negative on differences of two admissible projected likelihood signals for sufficiently small h
R3--R6: full physical copy-symmetric likelihood Gram is positive, extends analytically to all negative shifts, and has exact limiting normalized four-density dilation overlap
R8--R9: that overlap is at most C kappa^(9/4) exp(-c sqrt(kappa)), hence decays faster than the original sech(d) limit
R10--R12: no arbitrary nonzero node factors or PSD tensor multiplier can identify this exact Gram with original V on I, using analytic all-rank positivity propagation
